I wrote the pitch below, but I left out "proven hit." The game hasn't been published or sold yet, and 23 ratings is a small sample. Backers on crowdfunding sites, and especially board game backers, check claims like that. A first-time creator who overclaims loses trust fast, and the platform's rules on misleading statements could also apply. Your real numbers are strong for a first campaign, so the pitch uses them directly: 140 sessions, 60 testers, an 8.1 average and 1,240 sign-ups. That will persuade people more than a label they can't check.

<final_document>
**[Game Title]: Keep the Light Burning Until Spring**

The last supply boat has gone. The sea is freezing at the edges. Between now and the spring thaw, your family has to keep the lamp lit, the larder full and each other going.

[Game Title] is a cooperative board game for 1 to 4 players. You play a lighthouse keeper's family getting through one long winter. Everyone wins together or loses together. Every choice is a trade-off: oil for the lamp or fuel for the stove, mending the roof or watching the water. Storms come in, supplies run out, and the ships out in the dark rely on you.

It's a game about the hard things that happen in a small, close household. It works well as a quiet solo evening and just as well as a tense four-player night around the kitchen table.

**Tested Hard at Real Tables**

I've spent the past three years making sure this game holds up.

- **140 playtest sessions** since 2023
- **About 60 different playtesters**, from seasoned hobbyists to people who rarely play board games
- **2 conventions**, with strangers sitting down to play and giving honest feedback
- **An average rating of 8.1** from the first 23 players who rated it on BoardGameGeek
- **1,240 people** signed up to hear about this launch before it went live

Every one of those sessions changed something, whether a rule, a card or a balance tweak. The version you'll get has been through the hands of dozens of players who weren't shy about telling me what didn't work.

**Who's Making This**

My name is [Your Name]. I work full time as a land surveyor, and this is my first published game. I won't pretend to be a big studio. What I can offer is a game I've rebuilt dozens of times because I wanted it to be right, and a commitment to tell you plainly how the project is going at every stage.

**Where Your Money Goes**

The goal is **$28,000**. I already have a factory quote for a print run of 1,500 copies, and shipping costs are worked out. Reaching the goal covers manufacturing, shipping to backers and platform fees. Any money raised beyond the goal goes toward [stretch goals / component upgrades / a contingency buffer].

Throughout the campaign and production, I'll post regular updates with photos from the factory, so you'll always know where your copy is.

**Your Pledge**

**$49, with US shipping included**, gets you a copy of [Game Title]. [Add international shipping details and any add-ons here.]

**Help Keep the Light On**

Every pledge brings this game closer to the table. If you like cooperative games, stories that unfold over a single season, or games where every decision feels like it matters, I'd be honored to have you on board.

Thank you for reading, and for helping me get this family through the winter.

*[Back This Project]*
</final_document>

Some things to check before you launch:

- **Budget:** At $49, you need about 570 backers to reach the goal. At that level, printing ($17,400) plus about $5,100 in shipping plus roughly 8–10% in platform and payment fees comes to about $25,000. That leaves only around $3,000 for everything else. Make sure that covers freight from the factory, tariffs, warehousing or fulfillment fees, and storage for the roughly 900 extra copies. If any of those costs aren't in your quote yet, consider raising the goal or the price. Then change the "Where Your Money Goes" section so it only says what's true.
- **Name the site:** I assumed "the main ratings site" means BoardGameGeek. Change it if not.
- **Placeholders:** Replace the bracketed items with your details. A sentence or two about one of your specific mechanics would also make the game section stronger.
